Collections.summary: A workspace for one slide, and what everything else hangs off. `Kind` says which sort: `Personal` is one person's own for that slide, made the first time they open it, and `Session` is one people work in together. Deleting one only sets `Deleted`, since it holds everything in it, and its owner can bring it back.
Collections.make: `POST /collections/ensure` with `slideId` gets your personal one, making it if needed. `POST /sessions` with `slideId` starts a session, and can take its name, `maxEditors` and `editPolicy`.

CollectionId: The id everything in it points at
CollectionName: What it's called in the Collections panel. Sent when a session starts, otherwise made from your name. Can be renamed
Deleted: Set when it's deleted, so it's hidden. Never sent or taken over JSON
EditPolicy: `LastWriteWins` or `FirstComeWins` - what happens when two people change the same thing. A personal one stays `LastWriteWins`
Ended: Sessions only. Once set it's read only for everyone and its links stop working
MaxEditors: Sessions only. How many editors an edit link lets in before anyone else joins view only
Shared: Personal only. On, anyone signed in can look at it, read only
SlideId: The tiler's id for the slide. Not a foreign key - slides are files, not rows
UserId: The owner's Keycloak id, from their token. For a session, the host. They're in `CollectionMembers` as well

CollectionMembers.summary: Who's in a collection and as what. One row per person per collection, and what every access check reads.
CollectionMembers.make: Accepting an invite with `POST /invites/{code}/accept` adds you. The owner gets a row when the collection's made.

DisplayName: Their name then, from their token, so the panel can list people without asking Keycloak
UserId: Their Keycloak id. The other half of the key

CollectionInvites.summary: A link or code that lets someone into a collection, as a set role, until it runs out or is stopped.
CollectionInvites.make: `POST /collections/{id}/invites` with the `role` and how many hours it lasts. The store makes the code.

Code: What's in the link, and the key
CreatedById: Who made it, from their token
Expires: Now plus the hours asked for, up to a week
Role: What joining with it makes you. An edit link past `MaxEditors` lets you in view only
Stopped: Set when it's stopped early, so it stops working

AnnotationGroups.summary: A named set of annotations in one collection. One level only, and an annotation is in at most one. Deleting a group leaves what's in it, just ungrouped.
AnnotationGroups.make: `POST /annotationgroups` with `collectionId` and `name`, and optionally the annotation `ids` to put in it. Editors only.

Annotations.summary: One shape someone drew on a slide. The shape itself is fixed once saved - only the label, notes, colour and group can change. Going back through history only ever touches those four.
Annotations.make: `POST /annotations` with `collectionId`, `label`, `colour`, `shape`, `lineStyle`, `lineThickness` and `geoJson`. Editors only. `notes` and `groupId` are optional, and the group has to be in the same collection. `id` is optional too - the viewer sends its own, so it can draw the shape before the save comes back.

CreatedById: Who drew it, from their token
GeoJson: The drawn feature, in slide pixels, coordinates rounded to a tenth on save. Fixed once saved
GroupId: The group it's in, if any. Can change. Goes to null if the group's deleted
Id: Made by the store if it's left out
Label: client
Can change. Merged live with Yjs while it's being edited
Notes: Can change. Merged live with Yjs while it's being edited
Shape: `line`, `freehand`, `polygon`, `arrow`, `rectangle` or `circle`. The viewer can't show anything else, and the store doesn't check
SlideId: Copied from the collection, never taken from the client

CellCountGroups.summary: A named set of cell counts in one collection, the same as `AnnotationGroups` is for annotations. One level, and a count is in at most one.
CellCountGroups.make: `POST /cellcountgroups` with `collectionId`, `name` and optionally `cellCountIds`. An import can make them too, matched by name.

CellCounts.summary: A manual count of cells, such as mitotic figures: every dot placed, and the tally. The dots can run to tens of megabytes, so the Saved list gets `ColourCountsJson` and `PlacedByCountsJson` instead, and only `GET /cellcounts/{id}` sends the dots.
CellCounts.make: `POST /cellcounts` with `collectionId`, `label`, `dots` and `count`, and `regionOfInterest` if it was counted in a box. Editors only. Up to 80MB, about a million dots.

GroupId: The group it's in, if any. Set with `PUT /cellcounts/group`, not by saving the count. Deleting the group empties this
ColourCountsJson: How many dots of each colour, worked out from `Dots`. Null on rows older than this column until they're first listed. Not a change anyone made, so not in the history
Count: The tally. Can be more than the dots, since a click with `WithAnnotation` off counts without placing one
CreatedById: Who saved it, the host for a shared count
Dots: JSON array of `{x, y, colour}`, in slide pixels, with `placedBy` on a shared count. Fixed once saved
Id: Made by the store if it's left out
Label: client
Can change
LocationX: Where it was counted, for going back there. Null for a count with no location
PlacedByCountsJson: How many dots each person placed, the same way as `ColourCountsJson`
WithAnnotation: Whether clicks placed dots, or only counted
WithRoi: Whether it was counted inside a region of interest

RegionsOfInterest.summary: The box a cell count was taken inside. At most one per count, and it's fixed once saved. It goes when its count goes, and comes back with it.
RegionsOfInterest.make: Sent inside the cell count, as `regionOfInterest` with `geoJson`. There's no endpoint of its own.

CellCountId: Its count. The unique index is what makes it one to one
GeoJson: The box, rounded the same way as an annotation's

ImageAdjustments.summary: A saved preset of brightness, contrast, gamma and colour. Personal, so the viewer keeps them in your own collection whichever one you're working in, and putting a whole collection back leaves them alone.

AdjustmentName: What it's called in the list
ImageAdjustmentId: Made by the store if it's left out
UserId: Who saved it, from their token

history.ChangeSets.summary: One change someone made, like a commit - a single save, or a 21,000 row delete sent in batches under one id. Nothing can change a versioned row outside one.
history.ChangeSets.make: Made by any write. Send a `Change-Set-Id` header to choose the id, so several requests count as one change. Left out, the write gets its own. An id already used by someone else or in another collection is a 400.

Id: From the `Change-Set-Id` header, or made by the store
UserId: Who made it, from their token
What: What the first request in it did, such as `delete annotations` or `restore collection`
Source: Where it came from, when it's something sent in a message: who sent it, the message, the collection and how many of each it added. `What` is then `add from message`
SourceRows: Which row each new one was copied from. Apart from `Source` since it's two ids a row, and the History list reads `Source` for every line

history.Entries.summary: What one change did to one row, and the only place anything that was there is kept. A delete keeps the whole row in `Before`. An update keeps only the columns it changed, before and after. A create keeps nothing, since the live row has it, or a later delete's `Before` will. Column names are as they are in the table, so `Before` is the same as Postgres' `to_jsonb` of the row.
history.Entries.make: Never by hand. `HistoryLog` writes them with every save, in the same transaction, from what EF is about to change. Bulk changes go through `AnnotationBulk`, which writes its own with one `COPY`.

After: An update: the same columns, as they became. A group's delete in a merge: `{ "MergedInto": id }`
Before: A delete: the whole row. An update: the columns it changed, as they were
CollectionId: Copied from the change set, for reading one row's history. Not a foreign key of its own
EntityId: The row it's about. Not a foreign key, since that row may be gone
Id: Identity, so it's the order they were written in. Handed out before a save commits, so a higher one can be visible before a lower one

history.Snapshots.summary: What can change in a whole collection at one moment, so putting it back doesn't have to undo everything since. Shapes and dots are left out, since they never change: for 20,000 annotations it's 820KB against 25MB of whole rows. Only a shortcut - going back works without one.
history.Snapshots.make: Never by hand. `SnapshotService` checks every 30 seconds for collections with 5,000 entries since their last one.

Rows: Kind of row to row id to column to value
UpToEntry: The last entry that's in it. Not a foreign key
